name: Rage
desc: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor:
- You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
- When you make a melee weapon Attack using Strength, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level.
- You have Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
If you are able to cast Spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked Unconscious or if Your Turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on Your Turn as a Bonus Action.

Once you have raged the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a Long Rest before you can rage again. You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.
content: The Barbarian's Rage ability allows you to unleash primal ferocity in battle, granting advantages such as increased Strength checks and saving throws, bonus damage on melee attacks using Strength, and resistance to certain types of damage. While raging, you cannot cast spells or concentrate on them. The rage lasts for 1 minute and can be ended early, with a limit on the number of rages based on your barbarian level. A Long Rest is required to rage again after reaching the maximum number of times allowed at each level.

name: Unarmored Defense
desc: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.
content: Barbarian class feature: Unarmored Defense. At level 1, while not wearing armor, your Armor Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier + Constitution modifier. Can use shield and still benefit.

name: Reckless Attack
desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.
content: Reckless Attack is a feature of the Barbarian class which allows you to forego defense for a more aggressive attack strategy starting at level 2. By choosing to attack recklessly, you gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength, but also leave yourself vulnerable to attacks until your next turn. This feature enhances your combat capabilities by emphasizing brute force over caution, making it a valuable asset for Barbarians seeking to maximize their damage output in battle.

name: Danger Sense
desc: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
content: Danger Sense is a feature of the Barbarian class that provides an uncanny sense of danger at 2nd level. This ability grants advantage on Dexterity saving throws against visible traps and spells, as long as the character is not blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

name: Primal Path
desc: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Choose the Path of the Berserker or the Path of the Totem Warrior, both detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.
content: The Primal Path feature at level 3 for Barbarian class allows you to choose between the Path of the Berserker or the Path of the Totem Warrior, shaping the nature of your rage. This choice grants you features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

name: Frenzy
desc: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).
content: The Frenzy feature is part of the Barbarian class, specifically the Berserker subclass, and is available at 3rd level. This feature allows the player to enter a frenzied state during rage, granting them an extra melee weapon attack as a bonus action each turn while raging. However, using this ability comes at a cost - when the rage ends, the player suffers one level of exhaustion. This feature enhances the Barbarian's combat prowess by increasing their offensive capabilities, but requires careful management to avoid exhaustion.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Barbarian Ability Score Improvement: At 4th level and subsequently at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels, Barbarians have the option to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature allows for character customization and growth, enhancing their capabilities in combat and other challenges. The maximum limit for ability scores using this feature is capped at 20. This feature provides Barbarians with the flexibility to tailor their characters to suit their playstyle and optimize their performance in various situations.

name: Extra Attack
desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
content: The Barbarian class feature "Extra Attack" allows barbarians to attack twice instead of once when taking the Attack action at 5th level. This feature does not have any prerequisites and can be found at "/api/features/barbarian-extra-attack".

name: Fast Movement
desc: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.
content: Barbarian class feature: Fast Movement increases speed by 10 feet at level 5 when not wearing heavy armor.

name: Mindless Rage
desc: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.
content: The Mindless Rage feature is a Barbarian (Barb) ability that can be accessed at level 6 for the Berserker subclass (Bers). It grants immunity to charm and fear while raging, suspending any existing effects for the duration of the rage. This ability enhances the Barbarian's resilience and combat effectiveness, making them a formidable force on the battlefield.

name: Feral Instinct
desc: By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.
content: Feral Instinct, a feature of the Barbarian class, enhances your instincts at 7th level, granting you advantage on initiative rolls. If surprised at the start of combat and not incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn by entering a rage first. This ability provides a strategic advantage in combat situations.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Ability Score Improvement is a feature exclusive to Barbarians at level 8, allowing them to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level. This feature prohibits raising an ability score above 20.

name: Brutal Critical (1 die)
desc: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
content: Barbarian class feature: Brutal Critical (1 die) allows you to roll one additional weapon damage die for a critical hit with a melee attack at 9th level, increasing to two dice at 13th level and three dice at 17th level. This feature enhances your combat prowess and emphasizes the barbarian's brutal fighting style.

name: Intimidating Presence
desc: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.
content: The Barbarian's Berserker subclass ability "Intimidating Presence" at level 10 allows you to frighten a creature within 30 feet by using your action, requiring a successful Wisdom saving throw. The duration of fear can be extended by using subsequent actions, but ends if the creature is out of line of sight or over 60 feet away. If the creature succeeds on the saving throw, the ability cannot be used on them for 24 hours. This feature relies on your proficiency bonus and Charisma modifier, emphasizing your intimidating presence and ability to instill fear in others.

name: Relentless Rage
desc: Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.
content: Barbarian class feature: Relentless Rage (Level 11) allows you to endure grievous wounds during rage, making a DC 10 Constitution saving throw to drop to 1 hit point instead of 0. The DC increases by 5 with each subsequent use, resetting to 10 after a rest. This feature showcases the barbarian's resilience and ability to fight on despite severe injuries.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Barbarian class Ability Score Improvement feature at level 12 allows you to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1, with limits on maximum score of 20. This feature can be accessed at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19, providing flexibility in character customization and enhancing overall power and effectiveness in combat situations.

name: Brutal Critical (2 dice)
desc: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
content: Barbarian's Brutal Critical (2 dice) feature allows the player, at 13th level, to roll two additional weapon damage dice for extra damage on a critical hit with a melee attack. This feature builds upon the Barbarian class's combat prowess, enhancing their ability to deal devastating blows in close-quarters combat. The feature name, level requirement, and description highlight the Barbarian's brute strength and skill in battle, making them a formidable force on the battlefield.

name: Retaliation
desc: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.
content: Retaliation is a feature available to Barbarians at level 14, specifically the Berserker subclass. When taking damage from a creature within 5 feet, a Barbarian can react with a melee weapon attack against that creature. This ability showcases the Barbarian's resilience and combat prowess in close quarters.

name: Persistent Rage
desc: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.
content: In the Barbarian class, reaching level 15 grants access to the feature Persistent Rage. This ability allows the barbarian's rage to last until they are knocked unconscious or choose to end it, showcasing their fierce and unyielding determination in battle.

name: Ability Score Improvement

content: Barbarian's Ability Score Improvement feature allows the player to boost their chosen ability scores by 2 or distribute points among two scores by 1 each at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This feature prevents scores from exceeding 20 and is exclusive to the Barbarian class, enhancing their combat prowess and survivability.

name: Indomitable Might
desc: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
content: Indomitable Might is a feature for 18th level Barbarians, granting the ability to use their Strength score in place of the total for Strength checks if the total is less than their score. This feature showcases the raw power and resilience of the Barbarian class, emphasizing their physical prowess and ability to overcome challenges with sheer brute strength.

name: Primal Champion
desc: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.
content: Primal Champion feature for a level 20 Barbarian class enhances Strength and Constitution scores by 4, with a new maximum of 24. This feature embodies wild power and is accessible through the Barbarian class.

name: Brutal Critical (3 dice)
desc: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
content: Barbarian class feature Brutal Critical (3 dice) allows the player, starting at level 17, to roll three additional weapon damage dice for extra damage on a critical hit with a melee attack, enhancing damage output significantly. This feature showcases the Barbarian's prowess in delivering devastating blows in combat, making them a formidable force on the battlefield.

content: Barbarian's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to boost your character's ability scores at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels in Dungeons & Dragons. You can increase one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 each time. However, the maximum score cannot exceed 20. This feature is exclusive to the Barbarian class and can significantly enhance your character's capabilities as they progress in levels.

name: Spellcasting: Bard
desc: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Your spells are part of your vast repertoire, magic that you can tune to different situations.
content: The Bard class's (Bard) Spellcasting feature at level 1 allows you to manipulate reality through music, casting spells from a diverse repertoire to suit various situations. This feature, Spellcasting: Bard, emphasizes the harmonious blend of magic and music, showcasing your ability to shape the fabric of reality to your desires. With no prerequisites, this feature showcases the Bard's unique blend of creativity and mysticism, making them a versatile and enchanting spellcaster.

name: Jack of All Trades
desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.
content: Jack of All Trades is a feature available to bards at 2nd level, allowing them to add half their proficiency bonus to ability checks that do not already include their proficiency bonus. This feature falls under the bard class and is described as adding versatility to a bard's skillset.

name: Bardic Inspiration (d6)
desc: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.
content: The Bardic Inspiration (d6) feature of the Bard class allows you to inspire others within 60 feet, granting them a d6 Bardic Inspiration die to add to ability checks, attack rolls, or saving throws. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining uses after a long rest. The Bardic Inspiration die upgrades to a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. This feature showcases the Bard's ability to motivate and support allies in various situations, making it a valuable asset in combat and skill challenges.

name: Bard College
desc: At 3rd level, you delve into the advanced techniques of a bard college of your choice, such as the College of Lore. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th and 14th level.
content: The Bard College is a level 3 class that offers advanced techniques in bardic arts, specifically focusing on a bard college of choice like the College of Lore. This choice grants features at 3rd, 6th, and 14th levels, emphasizing the development of bardic skills and abilities. The Bard College is defined by its specialized curriculum and unique capabilities tailored to enhance the bard's performance in various situations.

name: Song of Rest (d6)
desc: Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.
The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.
content: The Song of Rest (d6) is a feature of the Bard class, which allows you to use music or oration to aid allies in regaining extra hit points during a short rest. At 2nd level, each friendly creature who hears your performance regains an additional 1d6 hit points when spending Hit Dice. The additional hit points increase to 1d8 at 9th level, 1d10 at 13th level, and 1d12 at 17th level, showcasing the progression of this ability. This feature emphasizes support and healing capabilities, making it a valuable asset for a Bard character focused on aiding their party during rests.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
desc: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
content: Bard class's Lore subclass grants the Bonus Proficiencies feature at level 3, providing proficiency with three skills of the player's choice upon joining the College of Lore. The prerequisites for this feature are none.

name: Cutting Words
desc: Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.

When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.

You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.
content: The Cutting Words feature is a Bard (Lore) ability available at 3rd level that allows you to use your Bardic Inspiration to subtract from an enemy's attack, ability check, or damage roll within 60 feet of you. This feature showcases your wit by distracting and sapping the confidence of your foes, providing a strategic advantage in combat situations. It is a powerful tool for manipulating outcomes and creating opportunities for yourself and your allies on the battlefield.

name: Countercharm
desc: At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it (no action required).
content: Countercharm is a feature of the Bard class at level 6, allowing you to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. By starting a performance, you and nearby friendly creatures gain advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. This effect lasts until the end of your next turn, requiring the target to hear you to benefit. The performance can end early if you are incapacitated, silenced, or choose to end it voluntarily.

name: Additional Magical Secrets
desc: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.
content: The Bard subclass Lore gains the feature Additional Magical Secrets at level 6, allowing them to learn two spells of their choice from any class. These chosen spells count as bard spells for the Lore subclass, but do not count against the total number of spells known. This feature expands the bard's spellcasting versatility and adds depth to their magical repertoire.

desc: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.
content: Font of Inspiration is a feature for Bards at 5th level, allowing them to regain all expended uses of Bardic Inspiration after a short or long rest.

name: Expertise
desc: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies to gain this benefit.
content: In the bard class, the Expertise feature allows a character to choose two skill proficiencies at 3rd level, doubling their proficiency bonus for ability checks using those skills. At level 10, two additional skill proficiencies can be chosen for this benefit. The available skills include Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Religion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Survival. This feature enhances a bard's versatility and effectiveness in various situations, emphasizing their expertise in a wide range of abilities.

desc: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

content: The Song of Rest (d12) feature from the Bard class provides a healing boost during short rests starting at 2nd level, granting an additional 1d6 hit points to you and your allies who spend Hit Dice to regain hit points. name: Wild Shape (CR 1/4 or below, no flying or swim speed)
desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to magically assume the shape of a beast that you have seen before. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

Your druid level determines the beasts you can transform into, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. At 2nd level, for example, you can transform into any beast that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that doesn't have a flying or swimming speed.

You can stay in a beast shape for a number of hours equal to half your druid level (rounded down). You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:

- Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.

- When you transform, you assume the beast's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.

- You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your beast form. Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as call lightning, that you've already cast.

- You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. However, you can't use any of your special senses, such as darkvision, unless your new form also has that sense.

- You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.
content: Druid class feature Wild Shape (CR 1/4 or below, no flying or swim speed) allows transformation into beasts seen before, with limitations based on druid level and duration. While transformed, retain alignment, personality, and mental scores, gaining creature proficiencies. Hit points, abilities, and equipment adjust accordingly, with spellcasting and special senses limited to beast capabilities. Maintaining concentration on spells is possible, but actions requiring hands are restricted. Features from class, race, or other sources can be used if physically compatible. name: Wild Shape (CR 1/2 or below, no flying speed)

Your druid level determines the beasts you can transform into, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. At 2nd level, for example, you can transform into any beast that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that doesn't have a flying or swimming speed.

You can stay in a beast shape for a number of hours equal to half your druid level (rounded down). You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:

- Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.

- When you transform, you assume the beast's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.

- You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your beast form. Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as call lightning, that you've already cast.

- You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. However, you can't use any of your special senses, such as darkvision, unless your new form also has that sense.

- You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
content: In Dungeons & Dragons, the Fighter class offers the ability Action Surge (2 uses) at level 17. This feature allows the player to take an additional action during their turn, beyond their regular action and bonus action. However, after each use, a short or long rest is required before it can be used again. content: Fighter class ability: Ability Score Improvement (ASI) allows a Fighter at level 8 to enhance one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1, with subsequent boosts at levels 4, 6, 12, 14, 16, and 19. This feature prevents exceeding a score of 20.

name: Survivor
desc: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.
content: The Survivor (Fighter - Champion) is a resilient class feature attainable at 18th level. This ability allows the player to regain hit points equal to 5 + their Constitution modifier at the start of each turn if they have no more than half of their hit points remaining, excluding when they have 0 hit points. This feature emphasizes durability and survivability in battle, showcasing the pinnacle of resilience for fighters.

name: Additional Fighting Style
desc: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.
content: In the Fighter class, at 10th level, the Champion subclass gains the Additional Fighting Style feature, allowing them to choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature. This feature_specific subfeature_options allows the Champion to select from options such as Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection, and Two-Weapon Fighting. This empowers the Champion with additional combat versatility and strategic capabilities in battle.

name: Unarmored Defense
desc: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.
content: Monk class feature: Unarmored Defense grants a level 1 Monk the ability to have an Armor Class equal to 10 + their Dexterity modifier + their Wisdom modifier when not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This feature has no prerequisites and is accessible via the monk-unarmored-defense index.

name: Flurry of Blows
desc: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.
content: Flurry of Blows is a feature belonging to the Monk class, specifically available at level 2. This ability allows the player to spend 1 ki point to execute two unarmed strikes as a bonus action immediately after taking the Attack action on their turn.

name: Ki
desc: Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Ki Points column of Table: The Monk.

You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class.

When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Ki save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
content: The Monk class, known as Ki, unlocks the ability to harness the mystic energy of ki starting at 2nd level. Ki points are used to fuel various features like Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind, with more features learned as you level up. Spending a ki point requires a short or long rest to replenish, with meditation needed to regain points. Ki features may require a saving throw, with the DC calculated based on proficiency bonus and Wisdom modifier.

name: Patient Defense
desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.
content: The Patient Defense feature allows Monks to spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action at 2nd level. This feature, part of the Monk class, enhances defensive capabilities during combat by granting additional agility and evasion.

name: Step of the Wind
desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.
content: The Monk class feature Step of the Wind allows you to spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, while also doubling your jump distance for that turn. This feature is available at level 2 and has no prerequisites.

name: Monastic Tradition
desc: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.
content: Monastic Tradition (MT) is a feature available to Monks (MNK) at 3rd level, where they choose a specific tradition like the Way of the Open Hand. This choice grants them unique abilities at different levels, including 6th, 11th, and 17th. This feature signifies the Monk's commitment to a specific path within their class, enhancing their abilities and combat prowess.

name: Deflect Missiles
desc: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect or catch the missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand and you have at least one hand free. If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a monk weapon for the attack, which has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.
content: Deflect Missiles is a feature available to Monks at 3rd level, allowing them to reduce damage from ranged attacks by 1d10 + Dexterity modifier + monk level when using their reaction. If the damage is reduced to 0, Monks can catch the missile and spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with proficiency using the caught weapon or ammunition as a monk weapon. This feature enhances the Monk class's defensive capabilities and agility in combat.

name: Open Hand Technique
desc: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
content: The Monk subclass Open Hand Technique at level 3 allows you to manipulate your enemy's ki with your own, granting effects such as knocking prone on Dexterity saving throws, pushing up to 15 feet away on failed Strength saving throws, and preventing reactions until your next turn after hitting with Flurry of Blows attacks. This feature enhances combat versatility and control for Monks specializing in the Open Hand tradition.

name: Unarmored Movement
desc: Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in Table: The Monk.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.
content: Monk class feature: Unarmored Movement grants a speed increase of 10 feet at level 2, with additional bonuses at higher monk levels. This ability allows movement along vertical surfaces and across liquids without falling at level 9. The feature is accessible through the url /api/features/unarmored-movement-1 and is exclusive to monks.

desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Monk class's Ability Score Improvement feature allows characters to increase one ability score by 2 at 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, or increase two ability scores by 1. This feature prevents ability scores from exceeding 20.

name: Slow Fall
desc: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.
content: The Slow Fall feature allows Monks to reduce falling damage by five times their monk level when falling, a skill acquired at 4th level. This ability is part of the Monk class and has no prerequisites.

name: Martial Arts
desc: At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two- handed or heavy property.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield:
- You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons.
- You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of Table: The Monk.

- When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.

Certain monasteries use specialized forms of the monk weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (called a nunchaku) or a sickle with a shorter, straighter blade (called a kama). Whatever name you use for a monk weapon, you can use the game statistics provided for the weapon.
content: The Martial Arts feature for the Monk class at level 1 grants mastery in combat styles using unarmed strikes and monk weapons like shortswords and simple melee weapons. Benefits include using Dexterity instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls, rolling a d4 for unarmed strike or monk weapon damage, and making a bonus unarmed strike when using the Attack action. Specialized monk weapons like nunchaku or kama can also be used with their game statistics.

name: Stunning Strike
desc: Starting at 5th level, you can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.
content: Stunning Strike is a feature of the Monk class at level 5 that allows you to disrupt an opponent's ki flow by spending 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike when hitting them with a melee weapon attack, causing them to make a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

name: Wholeness of Body
desc: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.
content: Wholeness of Body is a feature of the Monk class, specifically the Open Hand subclass, available at level 6. This ability allows the monk to heal themselves by regaining hit points equal to three times their monk level as an action, but requires a long rest before it can be used again.

name: Ki Empowered Strikes
desc: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
content: Monk class features: Ki Empowered Strikes (level 6) enhance unarmed strikes to count as magical, overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

name: Evasion
desc: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
content: Monk (Monk) at 7th level gains the Evasion feature, allowing them to dodge area effects with their instinctive agility. When facing effects that require a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, a successful save results in no damage, while a failed save results in half damage. This feature enhances the Monk's survivability and ability to avoid damage in combat situations.

content: Monk's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature, exclusive to the Monk class, prevents ability scores from exceeding 20.

name: Stillness of Mind
desc: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.
content: Stillness of Mind (Monk) is a feature that becomes available at 7th level in the Monk class. This ability allows the user to use their action to dispel any charm or fear effects affecting them. This feature has no prerequisites and is described as being able to end one such effect on oneself.

name: Extra Attack
desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
content: Monk Class (Monk) gains the Extra Attack feature at 5th level, allowing them to make two attacks instead of one when taking the Attack action on their turn. This feature does not have any prerequisites and is accessible through the monk-extra-attack index.

name: Circle of the Land
desc: The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.
content: The Circle of the Land subclass of the Druid class is known for safeguarding ancient knowledge and rites through an oral tradition, meeting within sacred circles to share primal secrets. Members serve as advisors to rulers and are influenced by the land where they were initiated. At level 2, this subclass offers subfeature options such as Circle of the Land: Arctic, Coast, Desert, Forest, Grassland, Mountain, and Swamp, allowing the druid to choose one feature specific to their environment. This subclass emphasizes wisdom, nature magic, and support roles within communities following the Old Faith.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Monk's Ability Score Improvement at level 12 allows you to increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1, at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This feature prevents exceeding an ability score of 20 and is part of the monk class's progression.

name: Tranquility
desc: Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.
content: Tranquility, a feature of the Monk class's Open Hand subclass, allows you to enter a peaceful meditation at 11th level, granting you the effects of a sanctuary spell until your next long rest. The saving throw DC is determined by your Wisdom modifier and proficiency bonus.

name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
desc: Starting at 13th level, you learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.
content: The feature "Tongue of the Sun and Moon" is a Monk ability that unlocks at 13th level, allowing the Monk to understand all spoken languages and be understood by any creature that can understand a language. This feature showcases the Monk class's proficiency in communication and empathy, enhancing their ability to connect with others on a deeper level.

name: Unarmored Movement
desc: Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in Table: The Monk.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.
content: The Monk class's Unarmored Movement feature at level 9 grants a 10 feet speed increase when not wearing armor or wielding a shield, with additional bonuses as monk levels increase. At this level, the monk gains the ability to move on vertical surfaces and across liquids without falling during the move.

name: Purity of Body
desc: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.
content: The Monk feature Purity of Body (PoB) grants immunity to disease and poison at 10th level, showcasing mastery of ki. This ability highlights the Monk class's focus on physical and mental discipline, enhancing resilience and fortitude in combat situations.

name: Diamond Soul
desc: Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and take the second result.
content: Monk class ability: Diamond Soul (level 14) enhances saving throws with ki mastery, granting proficiency in all saving throws and allowing spending 1 ki point to reroll a failed saving throw for a better result.

content: Monk's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your ability scores when you reach certain levels. At level 16, you can choose to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature can be used at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. However, the maximum ability score you can reach through this feature is 20.

name: Timeless Body
desc: At 15th level, your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, you no longer need food or water.
content: Monk (Monk) Timeless Body is a feature that grants immunity to magical aging at level 15, preventing frailty from old age. While you can still perish from aging, you no longer require food or water. This ability showcases the monk's resilience and self-sustainability, embodying the essence of inner peace and physical mastery.

name: Quivering Palm
desc: At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action.
content: The Quivering Palm feature of the Monk class (Open Hand subclass) allows you to inflict lethal vibrations on a target by spending 3 ki points when hitting them with an unarmed strike. The vibrations last for a number of days equal to your monk level and can be ended with an action, requiring a Constitution saving throw that can reduce the target to 0 hit points on a failure. You can only affect one creature at a time, and have the option to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action. This powerful ability showcases the deadly precision and control of a high-level monk.

name: Empty Body
desc: Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the astral projection spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.
content: The Empty Body feature allows Monks at 18th level to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute, gaining resistance to all damage except force damage. They can also spend 8 ki points to cast astral projection without material components, but cannot bring other creatures along. This feature enhances a Monk's stealth and survivability, offering powerful utility and defensive capabilities at higher levels.

name: Perfect Self
desc: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.
content: The Monk class's Perfect Self feature allows a character to regain 4 ki points at 20th level, when rolling for initiative with no ki points remaining. This feature has no prerequisites and is accessed through the /api/features/perfect-self url.
