This feature prevents scores from exceeding 20. This powerful enhancement is exclusive to the Monk class and plays a crucial role in shaping your character's strengths and weaknesses.

name: Fighting Style: Defense
desc: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
content: Fighting Style: Defense is a feature for Paladins at level 2 that grants a +1 bonus to AC while wearing armor. This feature is a part of the Paladin class and is related to the Fighting Style parent feature.

name: Fighting Style: Dueling
desc: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
content: The Paladin class feature Fighting Style: Dueling at level 2 grants a +2 bonus to damage rolls when wielding a melee weapon in one hand without any other weapons. This ability is part of the Fighting Style feature for Paladins, enhancing their combat prowess in close-quarters engagements.

name: Fighting Style
desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
content: The Paladin Fighting Style feature at 2nd level allows Paladins to choose a specialty in combat, with options like Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, or Protection. This feature can only be chosen once and offers unique benefits to enhance the Paladin's fighting abilities.

name: Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting
desc: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.
content: The Paladin class's Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting at level 2 allows you to reroll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a melee attack with a two-handed weapon, ensuring a higher roll. This feature is part of the Fighting Style parent feature and benefits from the two-handed or versatile property of the weapon.

name: Fighting Style: Protection
desc: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.
content: The Paladin class offers the Fighting Style: Protection at level 2, allowing the wielder to impose disadvantage on attack rolls against nearby targets when wielding a shield. This feature, part of the Fighting Style parent category, showcases the class's defensive capabilities and strategic combat skills.

name: Lay on Hands
desc: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level x 5.
As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.

Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one.
This feature has no effect on undead and constructs.
content: The Lay on Hands ability of the Paladin class allows you to heal wounds by drawing power from a healing pool that replenishes after a long rest. You can restore hit points equal to your paladin level multiplied by 5 by touching a creature and using your healing pool. Additionally, you can expend 5 hit points to cure diseases or neutralize poisons affecting a target. This feature does not work on undead or constructs, making it a valuable tool for healing and support in combat.

name: Divine Health
desc: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.
content: The Paladin class feature Divine Health (DH) at level 3 grants immunity to disease, showcasing the divine magic's influence on the character. This feature has no prerequisites and is accessed through the url /api/features/divine-health.

name: Sacred Oath
desc: When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose an oath, such as the Oath of Devotion.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.
content: The Sacred Oath is a feature available to Paladins at 3rd level, allowing them to swear an oath that binds them forever to their path. This choice grants them features at 3rd, 7th, 15th, and 20th levels, including oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature. As part of the Paladin class, the Sacred Oath signifies a commitment to a specific code or belief system that shapes their abilities and actions in combat and beyond.

name: Oath Spells
desc: Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.
content: The Paladin class's Oath Spells feature grants access to a list of associated spells at level 3. These oath spells are always prepared and do not count against daily spell preparation limits. If a paladin gains an oath spell not on the paladin spell list, it still counts as a paladin spell. This feature is essential for diversifying a paladin's spellcasting abilities and enhancing their combat prowess.

name: Divine Smite
desc: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.
content: The Paladin class feature Divine Smite allows a 2nd level Paladin to expend a spell slot to deal radiant damage on a hit with a melee weapon attack. The additional damage starts at 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot and increases by 1d8 for each higher spell level, up to a maximum of 5d8. This extra damage also increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.

name: Channel Divinity
desc: Your oath allows you to channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. Each Channel Divinity option provided by your oath explains how to use it.
When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.
Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your paladin spell save DC.
content: The Paladin class offers the Channel Divinity feature at level 3, allowing you to channel divine energy for magical effects. Your oath determines the available Channel Divinity options, each with specific instructions for usage. After using Channel Divinity, you must rest before using it again. Certain effects may require saving throws, with the DC being equal to your paladin spell save DC.

name: Channel Divinity: Sacred Weapon
desc: As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. If the weapon is not already magical, it becomes magical for the duration.
You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends.
content: Paladin (Devotion) at level 3 can use Channel Divinity: Sacred Weapon to imbue a weapon with positive energy, adding their Charisma modifier to attack rolls and granting magical properties for 1 minute. The weapon emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light beyond. This effect can be ended as part of another action, and ends if the weapon is dropped or the paladin falls unconscious. This feature enhances combat abilities and emphasizes the paladin's connection to divine energy.

name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Unholy
desc: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead, using your Channel Divinity. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
content: Paladin (Devotion) Channel Divinity: Turn the Unholy at level 3 allows you to use your holy symbol to turn fiends and undead within 30 feet, making them move away from you and unable to take reactions. This action lasts for 1 minute or until damage is taken. This ability showcases the Paladin's prowess in combating evil creatures with divine power, emphasizing their role as a righteous protector against the forces of darkness.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Paladin class's Ability Score Improvement feature allows a character to enhance their abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature prevents ability scores from exceeding 20 and is crucial for character development and customization within the game.

name: Extra Attack
desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
content: The Paladin class feature "Extra Attack" at level 5 allows you to attack twice when taking the Attack action on your turn. This feature is part of the Paladin class, which can be found at the url "/api/classes/paladin". The prerequisites for this feature are not specified.

name: Spellcasting: Paladin
desc: By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.
content: Paladin Spellcasting: At 2nd level, Paladins can harness divine magic through meditation and prayer, casting spells akin to clerics. This feature, Spellcasting: Paladin, is a core ability of the Paladin class, allowing Paladins to access powerful spells to aid them in their quests for justice and righteousness. This feature has no prerequisites and serves as a pivotal aspect of the Paladin's abilities at level 2.

name: Aura of Devotion
desc: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
content: The Paladin subclass Devotion grants the feature Aura of Devotion at 7th level, providing charm immunity to you and nearby friendly creatures within 10 feet. This feature expands to a 30-foot range at 18th level, showcasing the protective nature of the Paladin class.

name: Aura of Courage
desc: Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
content: Aura of Courage is a feature of the Paladin class that grants immunity to fear within a 10-foot radius at 10th level, expanding to 30 feet at 18th level. This ability enhances the Paladin's defensive capabilities and reinforces their role as a protector of allies.

name: Aura of Protection
desc: Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
content: Aura of Protection is a feature of the Paladin class that becomes available at 6th level. When activated, this ability grants a bonus to saving throws equal to the Paladin's Charisma modifier (with a minimum of +1) to the Paladin or friendly creatures within 10 feet. This bonus is only applicable when the Paladin is conscious. At 18th level, the range of this protective aura expands to 30 feet, further enhancing the Paladin's ability to shield allies during critical moments.

name: Divine Sense
desc: The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover. You know the type (celestial, fiend, or undead) of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the hallow spell.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.
content: The Paladin class feature Divine Sense allows you to detect celestial, fiend, or undead beings within 60 feet who are not behind total cover, as well as consecrated or desecrated places or objects. By opening your awareness as an action, you can sense the presence of strong evil or powerful good, knowing the type of being but not its identity. This ability can be used a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier before requiring a long rest to regain all uses. Divine Sense (DS) is a level 1 feature with no prerequisites, providing valuable information on nearby entities and locations for strategic decision-making.

name: Cleansing Touch
desc: Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
content: The Cleansing Touch feature is a Paladin ability that can be accessed at level 14. This feature allows the Paladin to end a spell on themselves or a willing creature they touch by using their action. The number of times this ability can be used is determined by the Paladin's Charisma modifier, with a minimum of once. The uses of this feature are replenished after completing a long rest.

name: Purity of Spirit
desc: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.
content: The Paladin subclass Devotion grants the feature Purity of Spirit at 15th level, ensuring constant protection from evil and good effects. This feature has no prerequisites and is accessed through the url /api/features/purity-of-spirit.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Paladin class feature "Ability Score Improvement" allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. You cannot raise an ability score above 20 using this feature. This feature is tied to the Paladin class and is especially useful for customizing your character's strengths and weaknesses throughout their journey.

name: Aura improvements
desc: At 18th level, the range of your auras increase to 30 feet.
content: The Paladin class reaches level 18 with the feature Aura Improvements, expanding the range of their auras to 30 feet. This enhancement does not have any prerequisites and is accessible through the /api/features/aura-improvements endpoint.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Paladin's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. You can choose to increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 each. However, the maximum ability score remains capped at 20 through this feature. This feature is specific to the Paladin class and emphasizes character progression and customization in Dungeons & Dragons.

name: Holy Nimbus
desc: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.
content: The Holy Nimbus feature is a powerful ability available to Paladins of the Devotion subclass at 20th level. When activated, the Paladin emanates an aura of sunlight, creating a 30-foot radius of bright light and dim light beyond that. Enemies within the bright light take 10 radiant damage at the start of their turn, while the Paladin gains advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead for the duration of the aura.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Paladin class's (Paladin) Ability Score Improvement at level 8 allows you to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1 at specified levels. You cannot exceed 20 in any ability score using this feature. This feature enhances a character's overall power and effectiveness in combat and other challenges.

name: Favored Enemy (1 type)
desc: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.

You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.
content: The Ranger class feature Favored Enemy (1 type) at level 1 allows you to select a type of favored enemy from a list including aberrations, beasts, celestials, dragons, and more, granting advantages on tracking and recalling information about them. You also gain proficiency in a language spoken by your favored enemies and can choose additional favored enemies at 6th and 14th level, reflecting your encounters during adventures.

name: Natural Explorer (1 terrain type)
desc: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.
While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.
content: Natural Explorer (1 terrain type) is a feature for Rangers at level 1 that allows them to excel in a specific type of favored terrain, such as arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When making Intelligence or Wisdom checks related to their favored terrain, they gain double proficiency if proficient in the skill. While traveling in their favored terrain for an hour or more, Rangers benefit from advantages like unhindered movement in difficult terrain, immunity to getting lost through non-magical means, heightened alertness to danger, and the ability to stealthily move at a normal pace when alone. Additionally, they can forage for twice the normal amount of food and track other creatures with precision. Rangers can choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

name: Improved Divine Smite
desc: By 11th level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage. If you also use your Divine Smite with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Divine Smite.
content: Improved Divine Smite is a feature available to Paladins at level 11, enhancing their melee weapon strikes with divine power. Upon hitting a creature, an extra 1d8 radiant damage is dealt, which can be added to the damage of Divine Smite if used in conjunction. This feature showcases the Paladin's righteous might and reinforces their role as a powerful melee combatant.

name: Fighting Style: Archery
desc: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.
content: Fighting Style: Archery is a level 2 feature for Rangers, enhancing their ranged weapon attacks with a +2 bonus to attack rolls. This feature is a subset of the Fighting Style category, specifically focused on archery skills. It does not have any prerequisites.

name: Fighting Style: Defense
desc: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
content: Ranger class feature: Fighting Style: Defense (Level 2) - While wearing armor, gain a +1 bonus to AC. This feature is a part of the Fighting Style parent feature for the Ranger class.

name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting
desc: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
content: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting is a feature of the Ranger class at level 2 that allows you to add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack when engaging in two-weapon fighting. This feature is a part of the parent feature Fighting Style.

name: Spellcasting: Ranger
desc: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.
content: Spellcasting: Ranger (2nd level) allows Rangers to harness the magical essence of nature, similar to a druid, to cast spells. This feature, part of the Ranger class, provides a unique spellcasting ability that enhances their prowess in combat and exploration. With no prerequisites, Rangers can quickly adapt and utilize their newfound spellcasting abilities to overcome challenges and protect the natural world. The spellcasting feature is a defining aspect of the Ranger class, granting them versatility and strategic options in their adventures.

name: Ranger Archetype
desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate, such as the Hunter. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.
content: The Ranger Archetype is a subclass for the Ranger class in Dungeons & Dragons. At 3rd level, players can choose an archetype, such as the Hunter, which grants them unique features at various levels. This subclass does not have any prerequisites and is accessible at level 3. The Ranger Archetype is defined by its distinct abilities and playstyle within the game.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Paladin class offers the Ability Score Improvement feature at level 12, allowing you to enhance your abilities by increasing one score by 2 or two scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This feature prevents scores from exceeding 20 and is crucial for optimizing character stats for combat and role-playing scenarios.

name: Fighting Style
desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
content: The Ranger class feature "Fighting Style" at level 2 allows you to specialize in a particular style of combat, with options including Archery, Defense, Dueling, and Two-Weapon Fighting. You can choose one Fighting Style option, which cannot be taken more than once. This feature enhances your combat abilities and contributes to your overall combat effectiveness as a Ranger.

name: Hunter's Prey: Colossus Slayer
desc: Your tenacity can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.
content: The Hunter's Prey: Colossus Slayer feature is a subclass ability for Rangers at level 3 that enhances their weapon attacks by dealing an extra 1d8 damage to creatures below their hit point maximum. This ability can only be used once per turn and is part of the Hunter subclass. It is related to the Hunter's Prey feature and provides Rangers with increased damage output against powerful foes.

name: Hunter's Prey: Giant Killer
desc: When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature.
content: Hunter's Prey: Giant Killer is a feature from the Ranger class (RNG) subclass Hunter (HTR) at level 3. This feature allows you to make a reaction attack against a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you after it hits or misses you, as long as you can see the creature. It is a part of the Hunter's Prey feature set (HPR).

name: Hunter's Prey: Horde Breaker
desc: Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.
content: The Hunter's Prey: Horde Breaker feature is a subclass ability for Rangers at level 3 in the Hunter subclass. This feature allows you to make an additional weapon attack on each of your turns against a different creature within 5 feet of the original target. It is an extension of the Hunter's Prey feature, providing Rangers with increased combat effectiveness and versatility in targeting multiple foes.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Ranger's Ability Score Improvement at level 4 allows you to enhance one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 every 4 levels thereafter. This feature, exclusive to the Ranger class, prevents exceeding a score of 20.

name: Primeval Awareness
desc: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot you expend, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number.
content: Primeval Awareness is a feature of the Ranger class that becomes available at level 3. When activated by expending a ranger spell slot, it allows the ranger to sense the presence of aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead within 1 mile (or up to 6 miles in favored terrain) without revealing their location or number. This feature enhances the ranger's awareness of the surrounding region, making it a valuable tool for tracking and detecting various types of creatures.

name: Hunter's Prey
desc: At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Colossus Slayer
Giant Killer
Horde Breaker
content: Hunter's Prey is a feature of the Ranger class, specifically the Hunter subclass, available at level 3. At this level, you can choose one feature from three options: Colossus Slayer, Giant Killer, or Horde Breaker. This feature allows you to specialize in a particular type of prey, enhancing your combat abilities in dealing with them effectively.

desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
content: In the Ranger class, at level 5, the Extra Attack feature allows you to make two attacks instead of one when taking the Attack action. This feature does not have any prerequisites and is accessed through the "ranger-extra-attack" index.

You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.
content: Natural Explorer (2 terrain types) from the Ranger class is a feature that enhances your proficiency in Intelligence and Wisdom checks related to favored terrains such as arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. At level 6, you gain benefits like unhindered travel through difficult terrain, immunity to getting lost without magical interference, heightened alertness to dangers while engaged in other activities, the ability to move stealthily alone at a normal pace, increased foraging yields, and detailed tracking abilities. Additional favored terrain types can be chosen at levels 6 and 10, making this feature a valuable asset for wilderness exploration and survival.

name: Defensive Tactics: Escape the Horde
desc: Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.
content: The Defensive Tactics: Escape the Horde feature from the Ranger class (Hunter subclass) grants the ability to impose disadvantage on opportunity attacks made against the character. This feature is part of the Defensive Tactics series, requiring a level 7 proficiency. This defensive maneuver enhances the character's survivability in combat situations and complements the Ranger's skill set.

name: Defensive Tactics
desc: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will
content: Defensive Tactics is a feature of the Ranger class (Ranger) subclass (Hunter) at 7th level, offering the choice between three options: Escape the Horde, Multiattack Defense, and Steel Will. This feature allows the player to choose one of these defensive abilities to enhance their combat skills and survivability.

name: Defensive Tactics: Multiattack Defense
desc: When a creature hits you with an attack, you gain a +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.
content: Ranger Hunter Defensive Tactics: Multiattack Defense is a feature at level 7 that grants a +4 bonus to AC against subsequent attacks from a creature that hits you in a turn. This ability is part of the Defensive Tactics feature within the Ranger class and Hunter subclass.

content: Ranger's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to increase one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels, with a cap of 20. At level 8, players can enhance their character's capabilities by strategically boosting their chosen attributes, contributing to their overall effectiveness in combat and skill checks.

name: Defensive Tactics: Steel Will
desc: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
content: Defensive Tactics: Steel Will is a feature from the Ranger (Hunter) class at level 7, part of the Defensive Tactics parent feature. This feature grants advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

name: Favored Enemy (2 types)
desc: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.

content: Ranger class feature: Favored Enemy (2 types) allows a Ranger at level 6 to choose two types of favored enemies from a list including aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, undead, or two humanoid races. This feature grants advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks for tracking and Intelligence checks for recalling information about favored enemies. Additionally, the Ranger learns a language spoken by favored enemies upon gaining this feature and can choose an additional favored enemy and language at 6th and 14th levels. This choice should reflect encountered monsters during adventures, enhancing the Ranger's abilities and knowledge.

name: Hide in Plain Sight
desc: Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage.

Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.
content: The Ranger class feature Hide in Plain Sight at level 10 allows you to create camouflage using natural materials like mud, dirt, and plants, granting a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks when pressed against a solid surface of equal size. Moving or taking actions requires recamouflaging for the bonus to apply again.

name: Multiattack
desc: At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Volley
Whirlwind Attack
content: Ranger Multiattack (Hunter subclass) at level 11 grants either Volley or Whirlwind Attack as features. Volley allows attacking multiple targets within range, while Whirlwind Attack hits all adjacent foes. This versatile ability enhances combat effectiveness for the Ranger class, offering strategic options for engaging in battle.

name: Land's Stride
desc: Starting at 8th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.
content: The Land's Stride feature from the Ranger class at level 8 allows you to move through nonmagical difficult terrain without extra movement cost and pass through nonmagical plants unimpeded. You also gain advantage on saving throws against magically created or manipulated plants that impede movement. This feature enhances the Ranger's mobility and resilience in natural environments, making them adept at traversing challenging terrain and avoiding hindrances posed by plant-based obstacles.

name: Multiattack: Volley
desc: You can use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range. You must have ammunition for each target, as normal, and you make a separate attack roll for each target.
content: Multiattack: Volley is a feature from the Hunter subclass of the Ranger class, specifically available at level 11. This ability allows the player to make a ranged attack against multiple creatures within a 10-foot radius of a chosen point within the weapon's range. Each target requires ammunition and a separate attack roll. Multiattack: Volley is an extension of the parent feature Multiattack, offering a unique and versatile combat option for players specializing in ranged attacks.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Ability Score Improvement feature for the Ranger class allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1. You cannot exceed a score of 20 using this feature. This feature is associated with the Ranger class and is available at level 12, providing a significant boost to your character's capabilities.

name: Multiattack: Whirlwind Attack
desc: You can use your action to make a melee attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target.
content: The Ranger subclass Hunter gains the ability Multiattack: Whirlwind Attack at level 11, allowing them to make a melee attack against multiple creatures within 5 feet simultaneously. This feature is an extension of the parent ability Multiattack and showcases the Ranger's prowess in combat, making them a formidable foe in close-quarters engagements.

name: Favored Enemy (3 enemies)
desc: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.

You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.
content: Ranger class feature: Favored Enemy (3 enemies) at level 14 grants expertise in tracking, hunting, and communicating with specific types of enemies. Choose from aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, undead, or two humanoid races for favored enemies. Gain advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks for tracking and Intelligence checks for information recall. Learn a language spoken by favored enemies. Select additional favored enemies and languages at 6th and 14th levels to reflect encountered monsters.

name: Vanish
desc: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.
content: Vanish is a feature for the Ranger class at level 14, allowing you to use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. You also become untrackable by nonmagical means, unless you intentionally leave a trail.

name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Evasion
desc: When you are subjected to an effect, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or a lightning bolt spell, that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
content: The Ranger subclass Hunter gains the feature Superior Hunter's Defense: Evasion at level 15, which enhances their Dexterity saving throws against damaging effects like a red dragon's fiery breath or a lightning bolt spell. With this feature, if the Ranger succeeds on the saving throw, they take no damage; if they fail, they only take half damage. This feature is an extension of the parent feature Superior Hunter's Defense, providing enhanced defensive capabilities for the Ranger class.

name: Superior Hunter's Defense
desc: At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Evasion
Stand Against the Tide
Uncanny Dodge

item.name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against the Tide

content: Ranger's Hunter subclass grants the Superior Hunter's Defense feature at level 15, offering a choice between Evasion, Stand Against the Tide, or Uncanny Dodge. This feature allows the player to choose one of these options for enhanced defensive capabilities in combat.

name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against the Tide
desc: When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature (other than itself) of your choice.
content: Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against the Tide is a feature for Rangers at level 15, belonging to the Hunter subclass. When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to redirect the attack towards another creature of your choice. This ability is an extension of the Superior Hunter's Defense feature and showcases the strategic and defensive capabilities of the Ranger class.

name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Uncanny Dodge
desc: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
content: The Superior Hunter's Defense: Uncanny Dodge feature is a level 15 ability for Rangers, specifically those of the Hunter subclass. This feature allows the Ranger to use their reaction to halve the damage from an attack when they are hit by an attacker they can see. It is an extension of the Superior Hunter's Defense feature, providing additional defensive capabilities to the Ranger. This ability showcases the Ranger's agility and quick reflexes in combat, making them more resilient against enemy assaults.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Ranger class's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to boost your ability scores by 2 or 1 at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19, with a maximum limit of 20. This feature is essential for enhancing your character's capabilities and is a key aspect of character progression within the Ranger class.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Ranger's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. You can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1, not exceeding 20. This feature is exclusive to the Ranger class and can be found at the 19th level. Enhance your character's attributes and skills strategically with this powerful ability.

name: Foe Slayer
desc: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.
content: Foe Slayer is a feature belonging to the Ranger class, specifically designed for level 20 characters. This ability allows you to enhance your attacks against favored enemies by adding your Wisdom modifier to either the attack roll or damage roll once per turn. This feature provides unparalleled hunting capabilities, granting you a strategic advantage in combat.

name: Feral Senses
desc: At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.
You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.
content: Ranger (RNG) class feature: Feral Senses at level 18 grants preternatural senses, negating disadvantage on attack rolls against unseen creatures and detecting invisible foes within 30 feet as long as not hidden, blinded, or deafened. This ability enhances combat awareness and precision, benefiting stealth and perception skills.

name: Fighting Style: Dueling
desc: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
content: The Ranger class feature Fighting Style: Dueling at level 2 grants a +2 bonus to damage rolls when wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons. This feature is a subset of the parent feature Fighting Style.

name: Natural Explorer (3 terrain types)
desc: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.
While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.
content: Natural Explorer (3 terrain types) is a feature for the Ranger class, available at level 10. This feature allows the Ranger to choose a favored terrain type from a list such as arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When making Intelligence or Wisdom checks related to the favored terrain, the proficiency bonus is doubled if using a proficient skill. While traveling in the favored terrain for an hour or more, benefits include not being slowed by difficult terrain, not getting lost except magically, remaining alert to danger while engaging in other activities, moving stealthily at a normal pace when alone, finding twice as much food while foraging, and learning details about tracked creatures. Additional favored terrain types can be chosen at 6th and 10th level.

name: Sneak Attack
desc: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.
content: Sneak Attack is a feature of the Rogue class, allowing you to deal extra damage with finesse or ranged weapons when hitting a distracted foe. At 1st level, you can add 1d6 damage to attacks with advantage, or without advantage if another enemy is nearby and not incapacitated. The extra damage scales with Rogue level, making it a crucial skill for stealthy, strategic combat.

name: Roguish Archetype
desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities, such as Thief. Additional archetypes are available in the original source material. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.
content: The Roguish Archetype (Rogue) is a subclass for the Rogue class at level 3, offering unique features and abilities to enhance your rogue skills. At this level, you select an archetype like Thief that shapes your rogue abilities, with additional options available in the original source material. Your chosen archetype bestows features at 3rd, 9th, 13th, and 17th levels, providing a distinct playstyle and enhancing your rogue capabilities.

name: Cunning Action
desc: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
content: Cunning Action (CA) is a feature available to Rogue class members at level 2. This ability allows them to take a bonus action in combat, specifically the Dash, Disengage, or Hide actions. It showcases their quick thinking and agility, enhancing their maneuverability and tactical capabilities on the battlefield.

name: Fast Hands
desc: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
content: Fast Hands (Rogue - Thief) is a feature available at 3rd level in the Rogue class, allowing you to use your bonus action from Cunning Action for tasks like Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks, disarming traps, opening locks, or using objects. This feature has no prerequisites and can be found at the url "/api/features/fast-hands".

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: In Rogue class, reaching 4th level unlocks the Ability Score Improvement feature, allowing players to increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This feature prevents raising scores above 20.

name: Second-Story Work
desc: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.
content: The Rogue subclass Thief gains the ability Second-Story Work at level 3, allowing them to climb faster without extra movement costs and increase their running jump distance by their Dexterity modifier.

name: Uncanny Dodge
desc: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
content: In the Rogue class, at level 5, the Uncanny Dodge feature allows you to use your reaction to halve the damage from an attacker's hit that you can see. This ability enhances your defensive capabilities by reducing incoming damage, making it a valuable asset in combat situations.

name: Thieves' Cant
desc: During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.

In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves' guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.
content: Thieves' Cant is a feature of the Rogue class, allowing you to communicate secretly through a mix of dialect, jargon, and code. This skill enables you to hide messages in plain conversation, known only to others who understand thieves' cant. Additionally, you can interpret secret signs and symbols to convey messages about danger, loot, or the nature of an area. Understanding thieves' cant requires four times longer to convey a message compared to speaking plainly, showcasing the complexity of this covert communication method at level 1.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Rogue's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 8th level and various other levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature cannot raise an ability score above 20 and is available to characters of the Rogue class.

name: Supreme Sneak
desc: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
content: The Supreme Sneak feature from the Rogue class's Thief subclass grants advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks when moving at half speed or less starting at 9th level. This ability enhances stealth capabilities significantly for skilled rogues, allowing for more successful covert maneuvers.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Rogue class's Ability Score Improvement feature at level 10 allows you to boost one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. You cannot exceed a score of 20. This feature enhances character customization and power progression within the Rogue class.

name: Reliable Talent
desc: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
content: The Reliable Talent feature allows a 11th level Rogue to excel in their chosen skills, granting the ability to treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 on ability checks where proficiency bonus is added. This feature showcases the Rogue class's finesse and expertise, enhancing their reliability and skill mastery.

name: Evasion
desc: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an ice storm spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
content: The Rogue class feature Evasion (level 7) allows you to dodge area effects by making a Dexterity saving throw, taking no damage on success and half damage on failure. This ability is particularly useful against elemental attacks like a red dragon's fiery breath or spells like ice storm. Evasion showcases the agility and reflexes of a Rogue, emphasizing their ability to avoid harm through quick thinking and nimble movements.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Rogue's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your character's abilities when reaching 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. At each of these levels, you can choose to increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1. This feature prevents you from raising any ability score above 20.

name: Use Magic Device
desc: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.
content: The Use Magic Device feature allows Rogue (Thief subclass) characters at level 13 to bypass class, race, and level restrictions on magic item usage. This feature enables improvisation with magical items, showcasing the character's deep understanding of magic mechanics.

name: Blindsense
desc: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.
content: The Rogue class feature Blindsense (level 14) grants the ability to detect hidden or invisible creatures within 10 feet solely through hearing. This ability enhances situational awareness and stealth capabilities, making the Rogue a formidable adversary in close-quarters combat.

name: Slippery Mind
desc: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.
content: The Rogue class's Slippery Mind feature enhances mental strength at level 15, granting proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. The feature has no prerequisites and is described as gaining greater mental resilience.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: In Rogue class, reaching level 16 unlocks the Ability Score Improvement feature, allowing you to enhance one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This feature prohibits increasing a score beyond 20. This enhancement is crucial for optimizing character attributes and skills in the game.

name: Elusive
desc: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.
content: The Rogue class feature Elusive grants the character unparalleled evasiveness at 18th level, preventing attackers from gaining advantage on any attack rolls as long as the character is not incapacitated. This ability makes the Elusive feature a valuable asset for Rogues seeking to maintain the upper hand in combat situations.

name: Thief's Reflexes
desc: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.
content: The Thief's Reflexes feature for the Rogue class (Thief subclass) allows a 17th level character to take two turns in the first round of combat, with the second turn at a lower initiative. This feature emphasizes ambush tactics and quick escapes, enhancing the character's agility and strategic advantage in battle.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Rogue class Ability Score Improvement feature at level 19 allows you to increase ability scores at 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels, by either 2 points in one score or 1 point in two scores, not exceeding 20. This feature enhances character customization and power progression, making it a valuable asset for optimizing character builds in the game.

name: Stroke of Luck
desc: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
content: The Rogue class feature Stroke of Luck allows the character at 20th level to turn a missed attack into a hit within range or treat a failed ability check as a natural 20. After using this feature, a short or long rest is required before it can be used again. This ability showcases the uncanny knack for succeeding when needed, emphasizing the Rogue's agility and resourcefulness in critical moments.

name: Sorcerous Origin
desc: Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, such as Draconic Bloodline.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.
content: The Sorcerous Origin feature is part of the Sorcerer class and is chosen at 1st level, defining the source of innate magical power, such as the Draconic Bloodline. This choice grants features at 1st, 6th, 14th, and 18th levels.

name: Spellcasting: Sorcerer
desc: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. This font of magic, whatever its origin, fuels your spells.
content: Sorcerer Spellcasting: At level 1, the Sorcerer class gains the ability of Spellcasting. This innate magical talent stems from a significant event in their past, passed down through generations, granting them the power to cast spells fueled by arcane magic. There are no prerequisites for this feature, which is detailed in the "Spellcasting: Sorcerer" section.

name: Dragon Ancestor: Black - Acid Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: Dragon Ancestor: Black - Acid Damage is a feature for Sorcerer class, specifically under the Draconic subclass at level 1. This feature allows you to choose a black dragon as your ancestor, granting you proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Draconic. Additionally, it enhances your Charisma checks when interacting with dragons by doubling your proficiency bonus. The feature is part of the Dragon Ancestor parent category.

name: Dragon Ancestor
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: Dragon Ancestor (DA) is a feature specific to Sorcerer (Sor) subclass Draconic (D) at level 1, allowing the player to choose a dragon type as their ancestor, influencing damage types and proficiency bonuses when interacting with dragons. The feature offers various options such as Black - Acid Damage, Blue - Lightning Damage, and more, each with unique attributes. Additionally, proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Draconic is granted.

name: Expertise
desc: At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit
content: The Rogue class feature "Expertise" allows the character to choose two skill proficiencies or one skill proficiency and proficiency with Thieves' Tools, doubling the proficiency bonus for related ability checks. At 6th level, two additional proficiencies can be chosen for the same benefit, expanding the character's expertise in areas such as Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Religion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Survival. This feature enhances the character's versatility and effectiveness in a variety of tasks, making them a skilled and resourceful member of the party.

name: Expertise
desc: At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit
content: Rogue Expertise (Level 6): Enhance your skills by choosing two proficiencies or one proficiency with thieves' tools at 1st level, doubling your proficiency bonus for related ability checks. At 6th level, gain this benefit for two additional proficiencies. Available options include Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Religion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Survival, and Thieves' Tools.

content: Dragon Ancestor: Brass - Fire Damage is a feature within the Sorcerer class, specifically the Draconic subclass, at 1st level. This feature allows you to choose a dragon ancestor, granting you abilities related to that dragon type throughout the game. By selecting Brass, you gain fire damage properties. This feature is derived from the Dragon Ancestor parent feature.

content: The Dragon Ancestor: Bronze - Lightning Damage feature is a subclass ability for Sorcerers specializing in the Draconic subclass at level 1.
