name: Dragon Ancestor: Green - Poison Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: The Sorcerer class's Draconic subclass grants the Dragon Ancestor: Green - Poison Damage feature at level 1, allowing the player to choose a dragon ancestor type that influences damage types and grants proficiency in Draconic language. This feature enhances Charisma checks with dragons by doubling the proficiency bonus. (Dragon Ancestor: Green - Poison Damage)

name: Dragon Ancestor: Silver - Cold Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: Dragon Ancestor: Silver - Cold Damage is a level 1 feature for Sorcerers with the Draconic subclass. This feature allows players to choose a dragon ancestor whose damage type affects later features. It grants proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Draconic, and doubles the proficiency bonus for Charisma checks with dragons. This feature is a part of the Dragon Ancestor parent feature.

name: Dragon Ancestor: White - Cold Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: The Dragon Ancestor: White - Cold Damage feature is a level 1 ability for Sorcerers specializing in the Draconic subclass. By choosing the White dragon as your ancestor, you gain the ability to use cold damage in your features. This feature also grants proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Draconic, as well as doubling your proficiency bonus when making Charisma checks with dragons. The Dragon Ancestor parent feature is the basis for this specific ability, allowing for a deeper connection to your draconic heritage.

name: Draconic Resilience
desc: As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
content: Draconic Resilience is a feature for Sorcerers of the Draconic subclass, enhancing their physical traits with dragon-like scales and increasing their hit point maximum at level 1 and subsequent levels in the class. This feature also boosts the Sorcerer's Armor Class (AC) when not wearing armor, providing a base value of 13 plus their Dexterity modifier.

name: Font of Magic
desc: At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.
Sorcery Points

You have 2 sorcery points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer table. You can never have more sorcery points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.
content: Sorcerer (Sorcerer class) gains the Font of Magic feature at level 2, tapping into a wellspring of sorcery points for various magical effects. With 2 sorcery points initially, more are gained as levels increase, following the Sorcerer table. Sorcery points cannot exceed the limit for each level and are fully replenished after a long rest. This feature embodies the sorcerer's innate connection to magic and their ability to manipulate it for powerful effects.

name: Flexible Casting: Creating Spell Slots
desc: You can transform unexpended sorcery points into one spell slot as a bonus action on your turn. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level. You can create spell slots no higher in level than 5th.
Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a long rest.
content: The Sorcerer class feature Flexible Casting: Creating Spell Slots allows a sorcerer of level 2 to convert sorcery points into spell slots up to 5th level as a bonus action. The created spell slots disappear after a long rest. This feature provides flexibility in managing spell resources and enhances the sorcerer's spellcasting capabilities.

name: Flexible Casting: Converting Spell Slot
desc: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one spell slot and gain a number of sorcery points equal to the slot's level..
content: This feature, Flexible Casting: Converting Spell Slot, is available at level 2 for Sorcerers. It allows you to expend a spell slot as a bonus action to gain sorcery points equal to the slot's level. This ability can be found under the Sorcerer class.

name: Dragon Ancestor: Red - Fire Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: The Dragon Ancestor: Red - Fire Damage feature is part of the Sorcerer class, specifically the Draconic subclass, at level 1. This feature allows you to choose a dragon ancestor, granting you the ability to use the associated damage type in future features. Additionally, you gain proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Draconic and have an advantage in Charisma checks with dragons. This feature is a variation of the Dragon Ancestor feature and focuses on fire damage.

name: Dragon Ancestor: Gold - Fire Damage
desc: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
content: Dragon Ancestor: Gold - Fire Damage is a Sorcerer subclass (Draconic) feature at level 1 that allows you to choose a dragon ancestor, granting you proficiency in Charisma checks with dragons and the ability to speak, read, and write Draconic. This feature is part of the Dragon Ancestor parent feature.

name: Metamagic: Empowered Spell
desc: When you roll damage for a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.
You can use Empowered Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.
content: Sorcerer class's Metamagic: Empowered Spell feature allows you to spend 1 sorcery point to reroll damage dice up to your Charisma modifier, using the new rolls. This metamagic option can be used even if another one has been used during the spell casting process. This feature is part of the Metamagic parent category and is available at level 3.

name: Metamagic
desc: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.
content: In Sorcerer class, Metamagic (Metamagic) is a feature that unlocks at level 3, allowing you to manipulate your spells with two chosen Metamagic options from a list that includes Careful Spell, Distant Spell, Empowered Spell, Extended Spell, Heightened Spell, Quickened Spell, Subtle Spell, and Twinned Spell. You can apply one Metamagic option per spell cast unless specified otherwise, granting you flexibility and strategic choices in spellcasting.

name: Metamagic: Extended Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
content: Sorcerer class ability: Metamagic: Extended Spell (Level 3) allows you to double the duration of spells lasting 1 minute or longer by spending 1 sorcery point, up to a maximum of 24 hours. This feature is a part of the Metamagic parent feature, enhancing spellcasting capabilities for sorcerer characters.

name: Metamagic: Heightened Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.
content: The Sorcerer class's Metamagic: Heightened Spell feature allows you to spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of a spell disadvantage on its first saving throw, making it easier to resist the spell's effects. This feature is part of the Metamagic category and is available at level 3, enhancing your spellcasting abilities by manipulating magic in subtle ways. With no prerequisites, this feature is a powerful tool for sorcerers looking to control the battlefield and ensure the success of their spells.

name: Metamagic: Quickened Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.
content: Sorcerer class (Sorcerer) gains the ability Metamagic: Quickened Spell at level 3, allowing them to spend 2 sorcery points to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action as a bonus action. This feature is part of the Metamagic feature (Metamagic), enhancing spellcasting efficiency and flexibility for sorcerers.

name: Metamagic: Subtle Spell
desc: When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.
content: Sorcerer class (Sorcerer) gains the Metamagic: Subtle Spell feature at level 3, which allows them to cast spells without somatic or verbal components by spending 1 sorcery point. This feature is part of the Metamagic (Metamagic) parent category and has no prerequisites.

name: Metamagic: Twinned Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).
To be eligible, a spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell's current level. For example, magic missile and scorching ray aren't eligible, but ray of frost is.
content: Metamagic: Twinned Spell is a feature available to Sorcerers at level 3, allowing them to spend sorcery points equal to a spell's level to target a second creature with the same spell that originally targeted one creature. This feature only works on spells that cannot target more than one creature at their current level. The Sorcerer class is known for its versatility and powerful spellcasting abilities, making this Metamagic a valuable asset for strategic spellcasting.

name: Metamagic: Distant Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double the range of the spell.
When you cast a spell that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 sorcery point to make the range of the spell 30 feet.
content: Metamagic: Distant Spell is a feature from the Sorcerer class that allows you to extend the range of your spells by spending sorcery points. At 3rd level, you can double the range of spells with a range of 5 feet or greater by spending 1 sorcery point, and you can increase the range of touch spells to 30 feet for the same cost. This feature is part of the Metamagic subclass and can be found at /api/features/metamagic-distant-spell.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: The Sorcerer class's Ability Score Improvement feature at level 8 allows you to increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1, at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. You cannot exceed 20 in any score with this feature, providing flexibility in character development and enhancing overall power.

name: Elemental Affinity
desc: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.
content: Elemental Affinity is a feature for Sorcerer class, specifically the Draconic subclass, at level 6. This feature allows you to add your Charisma modifier to damage rolls of spells matching your draconic ancestry's damage type and grants resistance to that type for 1 hour by spending 1 sorcery point. This enhances spellcasting abilities and emphasizes the connection between sorcery and draconic heritage.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Sorcerer class ability "Ability Score Improvement" at level 12 allows you to boost your chosen ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels, up to a maximum of 20. No prerequisites are needed for this feature.

name: Metamagic
desc: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.
content: Sorcerer Metamagic (MM): At level 10, gain the ability to manipulate spells with options like Careful Spell, Distant Spell, Empowered Spell, Extended Spell, Heightened Spell, Quickened Spell, Subtle Spell, and Twinned Spell. Use one Metamagic option per spell, with additional choices at levels 3, 10, and 17. Allows customization and flexibility in spellcasting for strategic gameplay.

name: Dragon Wings
desc: At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.
content: Dragon Wings is a feature available to Sorcerers of the Draconic subclass at level 14, allowing them to sprout wings for flight equal to their speed. These wings can be manifested as a bonus action and last until dismissed. However, armor not accommodating the wings may prevent their use. This feature enhances mobility and adds a thematic element to gameplay.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Ability Score Improvement is a feature exclusive to the Sorcerer class (Sorcerer) at level 16, allowing the player to enhance their character's ability scores at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels. This includes increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. However, the feature has a limit of not allowing scores to exceed 20. This feature emphasizes character customization and progression within the game.

name: Draconic Presence
desc: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.
content: Draconic Presence is a feature of the Sorcerer class, specifically the Draconic subclass, available at 18th level. This ability allows the sorcerer to channel the power of their dragon ancestor, emanating an aura of awe or fear within 60 feet by spending 5 sorcery points. Hostile creatures in the aura must make a Wisdom saving throw or become charmed or frightened until the aura ends, with immunity granted to those who succeed.

name: Metamagic: Careful Spell
desc: When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell's full force. To do so, you spend 1 sorcery point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell.
content: Sorcerer class feature Metamagic: Careful Spell allows you to protect creatures from spell effects by spending 1 sorcery point and choosing a number of creatures up to your Charisma modifier. This feature automatically grants chosen creatures a successful saving throw against the spell, making it a valuable tool for strategic spellcasting at level 3. This Metamagic is a part of the larger Metamagic feature, providing sorcerers with versatile options for manipulating spells in combat situations.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.
content: Sorcerer Metamagic (MM): At 3rd level, Sorcerers gain the ability to twist their spells using Metamagic options. They can choose one Metamagic option from a set that includes Careful Spell, Distant Spell, Empowered Spell, Extended Spell, Heightened Spell, Quickened Spell, Subtle Spell, and Twinned Spell. This feature allows Sorcerers to modify their spells for various effects, enhancing their spellcasting abilities at 10th and 17th levels. MM enables Sorcerers to adapt their spells to different situations, making them versatile and powerful spellcasters in combat and beyond.

desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Sorcerer's Ability Score Improvement feature allows you to enhance your character's abilities at 4th level and subsequently at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. This feature prevents exceeding an ability score of 20 and is linked to the Sorcerer class, providing a valuable way to customize your character's capabilities throughout their progression.

name: Dark One's Blessing
desc: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).
content: Dark One's Blessing is a feature of the Warlock class, specifically the Fiend subclass, available at level 1. When reducing a hostile creature to 0 hit points, the Warlock gains temporary hit points equal to their Charisma modifier + their warlock level (minimum of 1). This ability provides a strategic advantage in combat by bolstering the Warlock's defenses upon defeating enemies.

name: Pact Magic
desc: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells.
content: Pact Magic is a feature of the Warlock class, specifically designed for 1st level characters. This ability grants you proficiency with spells, enhancing your magical prowess through arcane research and the patron's magic. No prerequisites are needed to access this feature, making it a valuable asset for spellcasting within the warlock class.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
content: Sorcerer's Ability Score Improvement feature allows a character to enhance their abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th levels by increasing one ability score by 2 or two ability scores by 1. The maximum score limit is 20. This feature is specific to the Sorcerer class and is accessible at level 19.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Agonizing Blast
desc: When you cast eldritch blast, add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals on a hit.
content: Eldritch Invocation: Agonizing Blast is a level 2 feature for Warlocks that enhances the eldritch blast spell by adding the caster's Charisma modifier to its damage upon a successful hit. This feature has a prerequisite of knowing the eldritch blast spell and belongs to the Eldritch Invocations class feature.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Armor of Shadows
desc: You can cast mage armor on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.
content: "Warlock Eldritch Invocation: Armor of Shadows is a level 2 feature that allows you to cast mage armor at will on yourself, without using a spell slot or material components. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations category, granting Warlocks additional magical abilities."

name: Eldritch Invocation: Beast Speech
desc: You can cast speak with animals at will, without expending a spell slot.
content: Warlock (Warlock) class features the Eldritch Invocation: Beast Speech at level 2, allowing you to cast speak with animals at will without using a spell slot. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations (Eldritch Invocations) category, making it a valuable asset for communication with animals in your adventures.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Beguiling Influence
desc: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.
content: Eldritch Invocation: Beguiling Influence is a level 2 feature from the Warlock class, granting proficiency in Deception and Persuasion skills. It belongs to the Eldritch Invocations category and does not have any prerequisites.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Book of Ancient Secrets
desc: You can now inscribe magical rituals in your Book of Shadows. Choose two 1st-level spells that have the ritual tag from any class's spell list (the two needn't be from the same list). The spells appear in the book and don't count against the number of spells you know. With your Book of Shadows in hand, you can cast the chosen spells as rituals. You can't cast the spells except as rituals, unless you've learned them by some other means. You can also cast a warlock spell you know as a ritual if it has the ritual tag.

On your adventures, you can add other ritual spells to your Book of Shadows. When you find such a spell, you can add it to the book if the spell's level is equal to or less than half your warlock level (rounded up) and if you can spare the time to transcribe the spell. For each level of the spell, the transcription process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp for the rare inks needed to inscribe it.
content: Warlock Eldritch Invocation: Book of Ancient Secrets (Level 2) allows Warlocks to inscribe magical rituals in their Book of Shadows, choosing two 1st-level spells with the ritual tag from any spell list to add to the book without counting against their known spells. These chosen spells can be cast as rituals with the Book of Shadows. Additional ritual spells can be added when found, with the transcription process costing 50 gp for rare inks and taking 2 hours per spell level. Prerequisites include the Pact of the Tome feature, and the invocation is part of the Eldritch Invocations feature set. This powerful ability enhances a Warlock's spellcasting versatility and ritual capabilities.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Devil's Sight
desc: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.
content: Warlock (Warlock) class at level 2 gains the Eldritch Invocation: Devil's Sight from the Eldritch Invocations (Eldritch Invocations) feature. This allows the Warlock to see normally in both magical and nonmagical darkness up to a distance of 120 feet, providing a unique advantage in low light situations.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Eldritch Sight
desc: You can cast detect magic at will, without expending a spell slot.
content: Warlock class Eldritch Invocation: Eldritch Sight at level 2 allows you to cast detect magic at will without using a spell slot. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations category, providing powerful abilities for Warlocks.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Eldritch Spear
desc: When you cast eldritch blast, its range is 300 feet.
content: Warlock class Eldritch Invocation: Eldritch Spear at level 2 allows casting eldritch blast with a range of 300 feet, with a prerequisite of the spell Eldritch Blast. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations parent category.

name: Eldritch Invocations
desc: In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability.

At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. Your invocation options are detailed at the end of the class description. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn at that level.

content: The Eldritch Invocations feature from the Warlock class allows you to gain magical abilities at 2nd level, choosing from a variety of options such as Agonizing Blast, Armor of Shadows, and Beast Speech. These invocations grant you unique powers that can be swapped out as you level up, enhancing your spellcasting and combat capabilities. With options like Devil's Sight, Mask of Many Faces, and Thirsting Blade, you can tailor your character to suit your playstyle, whether focusing on deception, combat prowess, or utility. The Eldritch Invocations feature truly embodies the mystical and versatile nature of the Warlock class, offering a wide array of choices to enhance your gameplay experience and immerse you in the world of occult lore.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
desc: You can read all writing.
content: The Warlock class offers the Eldritch Invocation: Eyes of the Rune Keeper at level 2, allowing the character to read all writing. This invocation is part of the Eldritch Invocations feature.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Fiendish Vigor
desc: You can cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.
content: The Eldritch Invocation: Fiendish Vigor from the Warlock class allows you to cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell without using a spell slot or material components. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations and is available at 2nd level.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Gaze of Two Minds
desc: You can use your action to touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use your action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.
content: The Warlock class offers the Eldritch Invocation: Gaze of Two Minds at level 2, allowing the player to perceive through a willing humanoid's senses until the end of their next turn. While connected, the player benefits from the creature's special senses but becomes blind and deaf to their surroundings. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations parent category.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Mask of Many Faces
desc: You can cast disguise self at will, without expending a spell slot.
content: Eldritch Invocation: Mask of Many Faces is a level 2 feature for Warlocks that allows them to cast disguise self at will, without using a spell slot. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations class and is associated with the Warlock class. The feature has no prerequisites and can be found under the Eldritch Invocations parent category.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Misty Visions
desc: You can cast silent image at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.
content: The Eldritch Invocation Misty Visions allows Warlocks to cast silent image at will without using spell slots or material components, making it a powerful ability for creating illusions. This invocation belongs to the Warlock class and is part of the Eldritch Invocations feature, specifically designed for 2nd level characters.

name: Otherworldly Patron
desc: At 1st level, you have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being of your choice, such as the Fiend. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
content: The Otherworldly Patron feature is available to Warlocks at 1st level and grants features from a chosen otherworldly being, such as the Fiend, at various levels. This feature has prerequisites, includes abilities at levels 1, 6, 10, and 14, and is associated with the Warlock class.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Voice of the Chain Master
desc: You can communicate telepathically with your familiar and perceive through your familiar's senses as long as you are on the same plane of existence.
Additionally, while perceiving through your familiar's senses, you can also speak through your familiar in your own voice, even if your familiar is normally incapable of speech.
content: Warlock Eldritch Invocation: Voice of the Chain Master allows communication telepathically with familiar and perception through familiar's senses on the same plane of existence at level 2, with prerequisite feature Pact of the Chain. This feature enables speaking through familiar in own voice while perceiving, part of Eldritch Invocations parent category.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Mire the Mind
desc: You can cast slow once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
content: Eldritch Invocation: Mire the Mind is a level 5 feature from the Warlock class that allows you to cast slow once using a warlock spell slot, with the restriction of needing a long rest before casting again. This invocation is part of the Eldritch Invocations feature.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Repelling Blast
desc: When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.
content: Warlock class ability Eldritch Invocation: Repelling Blast allows the Warlock to push a creature up to 10 feet away in a straight line when hitting it with Eldritch Blast spell, at level 2 with a prerequisite of Eldritch Blast spell. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations parent category.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Thief of Five Fates
desc: You can cast bane once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
content: The Eldritch Invocation: Thief of Five Fates allows Warlocks at level 2 to cast bane once using a warlock spell slot, with a recharge after a long rest. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations subclass under the Warlock class, providing additional utility in combat scenarios.

name: Eldritch Invocation: One with Shadows
desc: When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible until you move or take an action or a reaction.
content: The Eldritch Invocation: One with Shadows allows Warlocks at level 5 to become invisible in dim light or darkness until they move or take an action or reaction. This feature is part of the Eldritch Invocations class and can be found within the Warlock class.

name: Eldritch Invocation: Sign of Ill Omen
desc: You can cast bestow curse once using a warlock spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Pact of the Blade
desc: You can use your action to create a pact weapon in your empty hand. You can choose the form that this melee weapon takes each time you create it. You are proficient with it while you wield it. This weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Your pact weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. It also disappears if you use this feature again, if you dismiss the weapon (no action required), or if you die.

You can transform one magic weapon into your pact weapon by performing a special ritual while you hold the weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. You can then dismiss the weapon, shunting it into an extradimensional space, and it appears whenever you create your pact weapon thereafter. You can't affect an artifact or a sentient weapon in this way. The weapon ceases being your pact weapon if you die, if you perform the 1-hour ritual on a different weapon, or if you use a 1-hour ritual to break your bond to it. The weapon appears at your feet if it is in the extradimensional space when the bond breaks.
If you serve the Fiend, your weapon could be an axe made of black metal and adorned with decorative flames.
content: The Warlock class offers the Pact of the Blade feature, allowing you to create a magical melee weapon as a pact weapon that can overcome resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. By performing a special ritual, you can transform a magic weapon into your pact weapon, which can be summoned at will. The weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you dismiss it. Serving the Fiend patron may grant you a unique weapon form. This pact boon is available at level 3 and is part of the Pact Boon feature.

name: Pact of the Tome
desc: Your patron gives you a grimoire called a Book of Shadows. When you gain this feature, choose three cantrips from any class's spell list (the three needn't be from the same list). While the book is on your person, you can cast those cantrips at will. They don't count against your number of cantrips known. If they don't appear on the warlock spell list, they are nonetheless warlock spells for you.

If you lose your Book of Shadows, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous book. The book turns to ash when you die.

Your Book of Shadows could be a weighty tome bound in demon hide studded with iron, holding spells of conjuration and a wealth of forbidden lore about the sinister regions of the cosmos, a gift of the Fiend.
content: Warlock Pact of the Tome (Pact Boon): At level 3, this feature grants the Warlock a Book of Shadows from their patron, allowing them to choose and cast three cantrips from any class's spell list at will without counting against their known cantrips. If lost, a replacement can be obtained through a 1-hour ceremony. The book, which can be a weighty tome of demon hide, holds forbidden lore and turns to ash upon the Warlock's death.

name: Pact of the Chain
desc: You learn the find familiar spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.
When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite.
Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its reaction.
Your familiar is more cunning than a typical familiar. Its default form can be a reflection of your patron, with imps and quasits tied to the Fiend.
content: The Warlock class offers the Pact of the Chain feature at level 3, allowing you to learn the find familiar spell and cast it as a ritual without it counting against your spells known. With this pact, you can choose special forms for your familiar such as imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite. Additionally, your familiar can make its own attack when you forgo one of yours during the Attack action. This feature is part of the Pact Boon family, reflecting a more cunning familiar tied to your Fiend patron.

content: Warlock Ability Score Improvement: At level 4, and subsequently at levels 8, 12, 16, and 19, Warlocks can enhance their abilities by increasing one score by 2 or two scores by 1. This feature allows for strategic customization of character attributes to optimize performance in various skills and abilities, with a maximum cap of 20 per score.

name: Fiendish Resilience
desc: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.
content: Warlock (Fiend) subclass feature: Fiendish Resilience grants resistance to a chosen damage type at 10th level, lasting until a different type is selected after a rest. This ability does not apply to magical or silver weapon damage.

name: Mystic Arcanum (6th level)
desc: At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
content: Warlock (Warlock) at level 11 gains Mystic Arcanum (6th level), a magical secret bestowed by their patron allowing them to cast a 6th-level warlock spell once without using a spell slot. This spell can be cast again after a long rest. Additionally, at higher levels, they can cast higher-level warlock spells in a similar manner: one 7th-level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level, regaining all uses after a long rest. name: Dark One's Own Luck
desc: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
content: Warlock (Fiend) subclass feature Dark One's Own Luck allows you to alter fate by adding a d10 to ability checks or saving throws at 6th level. This feature can only be used once per short or long rest, providing a powerful advantage in critical moments.

name: Hurl Through Hell
desc: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.

At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
content: Warlock (Fiend subclass) can unleash the powerful ability "Hurl Through Hell" at 14th level, transporting a hit creature through the lower planes, causing them to return after your next turn. This can only be done once before needing to finish a long rest. This feature is available at 20th level and has no prerequisites.

name: Spellcasting: Wizard
desc: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

This feature has no prerequisites and is accessible through the class index "wizard". Explore more about Spellcasting: Wizard at the provided URL.

desc: When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
content: The Arcane Tradition (AT) is a feature available to Wizards (Wizard class) at 2nd level, allowing them to specialize in one of eight schools of magic, like Evocation. This choice grants unique abilities at 2nd, 6th, 10th, and 14th levels, shaping their magical practice and enhancing their spellcasting capabilities.

name: Evocation Savant
desc: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.
content: Evocation Savant is a feature for Wizard class at level 2, specializing in the Evocation subclass. This feature allows for halving the cost and time required to copy an evocation spell into the spellbook. It enhances spellcasting efficiency and is beneficial for wizards focusing on evocation spells.

name: Sculpt Spells
desc: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
content: The Wizard subclass Evocation feature Sculpt Spells allows you to create safe zones within your evocation spells, granting a number of chosen creatures automatic success on saving throws and immunity to damage. This feature is accessible to level 2 Wizards and is a powerful tool for controlling the battlefield and protecting allies.

name: Overchannel
desc: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.
content: The Wizard subclass Evocation feature Overchannel at level 14 allows you to maximize damage dealt by 1st to 5th level damaging spells, with the risk of suffering increasing necrotic damage upon subsequent uses before a long rest. This powerful ability bypasses resistance and immunity, making it a high-risk, high-reward option for wizards focusing on spell damage output.

name: Arcane Recovery
desc: You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.
For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.
content: Arcane Recovery allows Wizards to regain magical energy by studying their spellbook. Once per day after a short rest, they can recover expended spell slots equal to or less than half their wizard level, with none being 6th level or higher. For example, a 4th-level wizard can recover up to two levels of spell slots. This feature enhances a Wizard's spellcasting abilities, providing them with more flexibility and sustainability in using their magic.

name: Spell Mastery
desc: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.
content: Spell Mastery is a feature available to Wizards at 18th level, allowing them to cast chosen 1st and 2nd-level spells at will without expending spell slots. Wizards can exchange these spells after 8 hours of study. This feature enhances a Wizard's spellcasting abilities by granting them greater flexibility and control over their magic repertoire.

name: Signature Spell
desc: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
content: The Signature Spell feature allows a 20th level Wizard to master two 3rd-level spells, casting them effortlessly without expending spell slots. These signature spells are always prepared and can each be cast once at 3rd level before requiring a short or long rest. If desired, the spells can be cast at higher levels by expending a spell slot. This feature enhances the Wizard's spellcasting abilities by granting mastery over specific spells, providing a powerful advantage in combat and utility.

This feature requires a long rest before reusing and all uses are restored after finishing a long rest.

name: Pact Boon
desc: At 3rd level, your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice.
content: Warlock Pact Boon at level 3 grants a choice of features from Pact of the Chain, Pact of the Blade, or Pact of the Tome, bestowed by the otherworldly patron as a reward for loyal service. This boon is a defining feature of the Warlock class, offering diverse options for enhancing gameplay and role-playing experiences.
